# Configuration reference

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_config_docs.py — do not edit by hand. -->

Every setting HomeHoard understands. This table is generated from the same
inventory the application validates against, so it cannot drift.

## Precedence

Highest wins:

1. **Explicit config** passed to `create_app()` (tests, embedding).
2. **Home Assistant add-on options** (`/data/options.json`).
3. **Environment variables** (`HBOX_*`, or `HBOX_*_FILE` for secrets).
4. **Built-in defaults.**

Home Assistant options outrank the environment because, inside the add-on,
options.json is the only surface an operator can edit — if the environment
won, toggling a switch in the HA UI would silently do nothing. Outside Home
Assistant the file does not exist, so the environment is authoritative.

An empty environment variable (`HBOX_AI_PROVIDER=`) means *unset*, and falls
through to the default rather than failing validation. The same applies to a
cleared field in the Home Assistant UI, which writes an empty string.

## Validation

Configuration is validated once at startup, before the database is opened
and before any port is bound. Invalid configuration prints **every** problem
and refuses to start — it never surfaces later as a request-time 500.

Booleans accept `1 true yes on` / `0 false no off` (any case). Anything else
is an error: an unrecognised value is never silently treated as false.

Check a deployment without starting it — this also prints which settings are
non-default and where each came from, which is the fastest way to answer
"but I set that option":

```bash
docker compose run --rm app python3 -m app.config_check
```

## Settings

### Storage

| Variable | Type | Default | Secret | HA option | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `HBOX_DATA_DIR` | string | `./data` | no | — | Directory for the SQLite database, attachments and persisted secrets. |
| `HBOX_DATABASE_URL` | string | `_(empty)_` | **yes** | `database_url` | Full SQLAlchemy URL. Blank = SQLite inside DATA_DIR. Postgres is supported: postgresql+psycopg://user:pass@host:5432/dbname. Supports `HBOX_DATABASE_URL_FILE`. |
| `HBOX_MIGRATE_FROM_SQLITE` | boolean | `false` | no | `migrate_from_sqlite` | One-shot: when DATABASE_URL points at an EMPTY Postgres and a local SQLite database exists, copy the SQLite data across at startup before serving. |
| `HBOX_USE_SHARED_POSTGRES` | boolean | `false` | no | `use_shared_postgres` | Home Assistant only: discover the Shared PostgreSQL add-on and use a database it provisions for HomeHoard. Ignored when DATABASE_URL is set. |
| `HBOX_POSTGRES_PROVISION_TOKEN` | string | `_(empty)_` | **yes** | `postgres_provision_token` | Token for the Shared PostgreSQL add-on's provisioning API. Leave blank to auto-obtain it via discovery; set it to the add-on's token if discovery can't supply it. |

### Security

| Variable | Type | Default | Secret | HA option | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `HBOX_SECRET_KEY` | string | `_(empty)_` | **yes** | — | JWT signing key. Blank = generated once and persisted in DATA_DIR. Deliberately has no add-on option: it must never be minted per boot, which would log every user out and void every API token. Supports `HBOX_SECRET_KEY_FILE`. |
| `HBOX_JWT_HOURS` | enum/int | `72` | no | — | How long an issued token stays valid, in hours. |
| `HBOX_DISABLE_AUTH` | boolean | `false` | no | `disable_auth` | Bind every request to a single local user. ONLY safe behind an authenticating proxy such as Home Assistant ingress. |
| `HBOX_ALLOW_REGISTRATION` | boolean | `true` | no | `allow_registration` | Allow anyone who can reach the app to create an account. |
| `HBOX_MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH` | enum/int | `8` | no | — | Minimum password length enforced on register / change-password. |

### Network & proxy

| Variable | Type | Default | Secret | HA option | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `HBOX_PORT` | enum/int | `7745` | no | — | HTTP port for the app. |
| `HBOX_CORS_ORIGINS` | list | `_(empty)_` | no | — | Comma-separated origins allowed to make credentialed cross-origin requests. Empty = same-origin only (correct for normal deployments). |
| `HBOX_PROXY_HOPS` | enum/int | `0` | no | — | How many reverse proxies sit in front. 0 = do not trust X-Forwarded-* headers at all. |
| `HBOX_RATELIMIT_ENABLED` | boolean | `true` | no | — | Enable request rate limiting (disabled automatically under tests). |
| `HBOX_PUBLIC_URL` | string | `_(empty)_` | no | `public_url` | The URL this HomeHoard is reachable at from your phone/browser (e.g. https://ha.example.com/api/hassio_ingress/<token> or a direct port URL). When set, notification digests append tap-through links to the Restock / Checked-out / Maintenance pages. Blank = plain-text digests with no links. |

| `HBOX_OLLAMA_SEARCH_KEY` | string | `_(empty)_` | **yes** | `ollama_search_key` | Ollama API key (ollama.com) for the hosted web search, used to enrich items with a short searchable description. Blank = enrichment is off. Supports `HBOX_OLLAMA_SEARCH_KEY_FILE`. |
| `HBOX_OLLAMA_CLOUD_API_KEY` | string | `_(empty)_` | **yes** | — | API key for Ollama Cloud (ollama.com), a distinct provider from a local Ollama server. Supports `HBOX_OLLAMA_CLOUD_API_KEY_FILE`. |
| `HBOX_OLLAMA_CLOUD_MODEL` | string | `_(empty)_` | no | — | Model for the ollama_cloud provider. |

### MCP (Home Assistant Assist)

| Variable | Type | Default | Secret | HA option | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `HBOX_MCP_ENABLED` | boolean | `true` | no | `enable_mcp` | Run the MCP server so Home Assistant Assist can use HomeHoard as a tool. |
| `HBOX_MCP_HOST` | string | `0.0.0.0` | no | — | Bind address for the MCP server. |
| `HBOX_MCP_PORT` | enum/int | `7766` | no | — | Port for the MCP server (SSE). |
| `HBOX_MCP_API` | string | `_(empty)_` | no | — | Backend API URL the MCP server calls. Blank = derived from PORT. |
| `HBOX_MCP_API_TOKEN` | string | `_(empty)_` | **yes** | — | Token the MCP server uses when app auth is enabled. Supports `HBOX_MCP_API_TOKEN_FILE`. |
| `HBOX_MCP_SERVER_TOKEN` | string | `_(empty)_` | **yes** | — | Bearer token Home Assistant must present to reach the MCP server. Blank leaves it unauthenticated (only safe on a trusted network). Supports `HBOX_MCP_SERVER_TOKEN_FILE`. |
| `HBOX_MCP_EXPOSE_EXTERNAL` | boolean | `false` | no | `mcp_expose_external` | Reach the MCP server from OUTSIDE Home Assistant. When on, every request must present a Full- or MCP-scoped API key, and the server refuses to start until such a key exists — so it is never open. You must also map the MCP port in the add-on's Network tab. |
| `HBOX_MCP_DEBUG_TOOLS` | boolean | `false` | no | `mcp_debug_tools` | Expose read-only debugging tools over MCP (recent logs, error summary, metrics, diagnostics) so an AI client can investigate a problem. Off by default. When on, those tools require an API key with the 'debug' scope — ALWAYS, including on the Home Assistant network, because logs contain login emails and tracebacks that can carry a database password. No debug key exists = the tools are not served at all. |

| Variable | Type | Default | Secret | HA option | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `HBOX_WORKER_ENABLED` | boolean | `true` | no | — | Run the in-process background-job worker thread (async AI tooling). |
| `HBOX_MAX_UPLOAD_MB` | enum/int | `50` | no | — | Maximum upload size in MB. |
| `HBOX_FRONTEND_DIST` | string | `_(empty)_` | no | — | Path to the built SPA. Blank = the location baked into the image. |
| `HBOX_DISCOVERY_HOST` | string | `_(empty)_` | no | — | Override the hostname advertised to Home Assistant via Supervisor discovery. Blank = ask the Supervisor for the add-on's own hostname. |
| `HBOX_DEBUG` | boolean | `false` | no | — | Flask debug mode. NEVER enable in production — it exposes an interactive debugger that executes arbitrary code. |

### Logging

| Variable | Type | Default | Secret | HA option | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `HBOX_LOG_LEVEL` | enum/int | `INFO` | no | `log_level` | Application log level. Applies to both the app and gunicorn. |
| `HBOX_SLOW_REQUEST_MS` | enum/int | `1000` | no | — | Log a line for any request slower than this many milliseconds. 0 logs every request, which fills the log on a busy instance — the gunicorn access log already covers the ordinary case. |

## Security notes

- **`HBOX_SECRET_KEY`** must be at least 32 characters when
  authentication is enabled, and known placeholders are rejected outright.
  Leave it unset and HomeHoard generates one **once** and persists it to
  `$HBOX_DATA_DIR/.secret_key` (mode 0600). Back that file up with your data:
  losing it logs everyone out and voids every issued API token. It has no
  add-on option on purpose — a key that changed per boot would do exactly
  that on every restart.
- **`HBOX_DISABLE_AUTH=true` binds every request to one local user.** It is
  correct behind Home Assistant ingress and wrong anywhere else. Combining it
  with `HBOX_CORS_ORIGINS` is refused outright, because that would let any
  listed website drive the API as that user.
- **CORS is same-origin by default.** The SPA is served by the app itself, so
  no cross-origin access is needed. Only add origins for a separate frontend
  (e.g. the Vite dev server at `http://localhost:5173`). `*` is refused.
- **`X-Forwarded-*` headers are ignored** unless `HBOX_PROXY_HOPS` says how
  many proxies are in front. Trusting them by default would let any client
  spoof its IP and evade rate limiting.
- **`HBOX_MCP_EXPOSE_EXTERNAL`** makes the MCP server reachable from outside
  Home Assistant. It is fail-closed: the server refuses to start unless a
  Full- or MCP-scoped API key already exists, so it is never open.
- **`HBOX_DATABASE_URL` is a secret** — it embeds the database password.
  It is redacted everywhere HomeHoard reports configuration.

## Deployment support

- **Docker secrets**: any setting marked `Supports HBOX_*_FILE` can be read
  from a file instead, e.g. `HBOX_SECRET_KEY_FILE=/run/secrets/homehoard_key`.
- **Home Assistant add-on**: set options in the add-on's Configuration tab.
  The `HA option` column above gives the key name.
